items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: And I played with a band called Harry Comet.

ctx.x: If you don’t mind just relating some of those, about the wedding?

Oh yeah when we were kids coming up in so-called musically, we were still in high school, and you know there was no rock & roll or Pop music as we know it today. It was all jazz and big bands, dance bands, you know like Vaughn Monroe, Jimmy Dorsey, Tommy Dorsey, Benny Goodman. They were jazz players but they were primarily dance bands. And people danced to the music. And so when we were in high school, he was in Paterson, I was in Ridgewood, our paths didn’t cross yet. And I played with a band called Harry Comet.…

Nobody had any money, the depression wasn’t even over yet. And that’s the way we learned to how to play, by playing all kinds of job. Now I think you were referring to the job about the wedding that came up? Bucky and I were playing an Italian wedding at a place called the Lafayette Friend’s Club in East Paterson. And I played there a lot, he played there a lot, sometimes we played together there. And this time we did. And I forget whose band it was. Anyway in those days the weddings were not glamorous like they…
